Yes, and `REV` already works that way: it can be any one commit. The merge's first parent is exactly what you name, whether that's `main`, `main@origin`, a change id, a commit id, or an `@` form. The branch is measured against it (`REV..@-`), so naming a node other than the fork point is fine.

Taking that one step further removes my open question entirely: let the presence of `REV` decide the shape, instead of counting commits.
- **`--closing <REV>`:** always the closing commit, the merge of `REV` and `@-`. That covers any node as the parent, for a branch of any length, a one-commit branch included if that's what you ask for.
- **`--closing` with no value:** always finalize `@-` in place, the single-step case with no parent. The cycle title is read from `@-` (an opening, its " opening" removed), or taken from `--title`.

What that gets you:
- **No hidden rule:** what you type decides the shape, and nothing has to be refused. A `REV` on a one-commit branch is just a request for a merge.
- **No counting:** the code needs no "how many commits above `REV`" logic. That logic is the one place `REV`'s choice could silently change the shape.
- **Your earlier wording still holds,** read as "a single-step closing has no parent, so it takes no `REV`; a multi-step one needs a parent, so it takes one".

It does reverse the commit-count rule recorded earlier ("a branch with one node is single-step"). The proposal section **A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count** would become "the closing's shape is whether it names a parent". The old Cycle shape rule, that a ladder of one closes as a ladder, would then be a choice you make by passing `REV`, not something the tool forces.

content.text:
That tool mostly exists already: `vc-x1 merge --target <REV> --from <REV>...` adds parents to any commit, keeping its description, change id, and `ochid:` trailer. It refuses only a cycle, a source at or below the target, and jj-immutable targets, unless `--ignore-immutable` is given. `commit --closing` itself is built on it. So "add a parent to a committed node, to fix something" is covered.

The gap is the other direction: `merge` only adds. Its own doc sends you to raw `jj rebase -r <target> -o ...` to remove or replace a parent. That's exactly the kind of hand-typed `jj` this cycle removes, so a `reparent` belongs in the plan: `vc-x1 reparent --target <REV> --parents <REV>...` sets the parents outright, with the same guards and the change id and trailer kept. With `merge` for adding and `reparent` for setting, any parent fix-up is a vc-x1 command.

That also settles `--closing`. It isn't a repair tool, so it can follow your original intent strictly:
- **`--closing` with no value:** a single-step cycle. `@-` is finalized in place, and it must be an opening, unless `--title` is given. With a rung there instead, it's refused with "a multi-step closing needs `--closing <REV>`".
- **`--closing <REV>`:** a multi-step cycle. The closing commit merges `REV`, any node, and `@-`. If there's only the opening above `REV`, it's refused with "one commit above `REV` is a single-step cycle: `--closing` with no `REV` finalizes it". `--dead-end` is the exception: a dead end keeps its opening and gets a closing commit even then.
- **Fixing a mistake** afterwards, such as a closing made against the wrong parent, is `merge` or `reparent` on the committed node. It isn't `commit` again.

I'd add `reparent` as its own rung next to the reshape rung. Shall I record both in the plan: the `--closing [REV]` rules for this rung, and **feat: vc-x1 reparent sets a commit's parents**?

message.content: How can we "unparent"? (Using the `merge` is the wrong "verb" and doesn't feel right, it merges commits.)

lastPrompt: How can we "unparent"? (Using the `merge` is the wrong "verb" and doesn't feel right, it merges commits.)

content.text:
With a command for the commit's parent list, not borrowing `merge`'s verb. One command covers adding, removing, and replacing:

```
vc-x1 reparent --target <REV> --add <REV>...      # what `merge` does today
vc-x1 reparent --target <REV> --remove <REV>...   # unparent
vc-x1 reparent --target <REV> --set <REV>...      # replace the whole list
```

What every form shares:
- **The target is any committed node** (not the working copy), and it keeps its description, change id, and `ochid:` trailer, as `merge` does now.
- **One jj-lib rebase** of the target onto its new parent list, with descendants rebased after it, snapshot-restored if it fails, and printing the parent list before and after.
- **The same guards `merge` has:** no cycle, no parent at or below the target, and a jj-immutable target needs `--ignore-immutable`.

What's specific to `--remove`, which is what makes unparenting different from merging:
- **The tree changes.** The target keeps its own diff, but whatever the removed parent brought in is no longer in the target's tree. Taking `main` off a closing merge, for example, leaves the closing sitting on the ladder alone. That's the point of a fix-up, but it's worth saying, so `--remove` prints what was dropped.
- **The last parent can't be removed.** A commit needs at least one parent, so removing them all is refused and points at `--set`.
- **A conflicted result** is reported and left as is, the way `merge` already handles it.

**What happens to `merge`:** adding a parent really is a merge in version-control terms, so the command isn't wrong, just narrower. I'd keep it as a short form of `reparent --add`, so its tests and its use inside `commit --closing` stay as they are. If one verb for every parent edit is what you'd prefer, it can retire into `reparent` later.

The plain version: `reparent` is the one tool for a commit's parents, `--add`, `--remove`, or `--set`, and `--remove` is the unparent, with the caveat that the commit then loses what that parent contributed.

    version stayed in the working copy for this rung to carry. They return once this rung pushes.

    needs the `--closing <REV>` code.

    made, which stays local until its review and the next `push` publishes it. At `@-` the push

    Opening step 2 does by hand. This replaces the first call, the bookmark created on the opening
    for the next push, since wink wants the bookmark pushed by `--opening`.

    (2026-10-23), a rung inserted after a live test left it off.
  - The line's bookmark advances to each work commit, locally, wink's call at the opening rung
    (2026-10-23), the remote moving only at `push`, resolved as `push` resolves it, `--bookmark`
    naming it and `--no-advance` leaving it.
  - `--skip` names the step left out, settled at the opening rung: `local` skips the creation, so
    the bookmark must be at `@-` already and is pushed, `remote` skips the push, and `both` skips
    both and only checks it is at `@-`.

    `--closing` appends " closing" on a ladder and nothing for a single-step cycle, a title already
    carrying the suffix refused so it is never doubled. `--dead-end` with `--closing` appends
    " dead-end closing".

  straight history, a linear closing is a plain commit on the ladder, and `--land` fast-forwards
  `REV` to it, the agent-files' keep separate under a clearer name.
  - `--shape <trapezoid|linear>` chooses it, one valued flag rather than `--linear` and
    `--trapezoid`, which could both be given, or abbreviations such as `--clse-lin`, which read as
    typos. The flag's word and the config key's are the same.
  - `[cycle] closing-shape`, `"trapezoid"` or `"linear"`, is the project's default, a preference
    that belongs in the committed `.vc-config.md` with `[validate]` and `[build]`, since adopters
    choose differently. Absent, it is trapezoid, so an adopter who sets nothing sees no change.
  - The flag, then the key, then trapezoid, and `commit` prints which decided. Close-out step 5
    still has the user choose, the key only making the usual answer the default, and a stated
    preference is not the assumption about the current branch that `--closing <REV>` removed.
  - Either converts to the other while the closing is a draft, before Land, by re-parenting the
    same closing, which keeps its change id and trailer, and with the trunk unmoved its tree too,
    `REV` being in the ladder's ancestry. After Land a conversion would rewrite the trunk, so it is
    refused.
  - A linear closing cannot join a trunk that moved: the ladder would need a rebase, a rewrite of
    published commits into a tree no validation saw. `--land` already refuses a moved trunk, so
    the refusal is the whole answer, and the way out is the reshape rung's command, then a
    validation, then the closing. A rebase inside a linear closing would be the hidden multi-step
    operation this cycle removes.
  - The v0.3.1 proposal said keep separate goes, and its section **The closing is a trapezoid or
    linear, and converts** now keeps it as the linear shape and names the flag and the key, edited
    at the closing rung's review when this rung was added, so the proposal leads the flag by one
    rung.
  - Its own rung after the closing's shapes, since `--land` lands both.
- `commit --closing <REV> --land`, wink's call (2026-10-23): Land needs no review of its own, so
  the closing and its Land are one invocation under the one go given at the closing's description
  review.
  - The per-rung flow already reviews everything the closing carries, its working-copy diff at
    step 6 and its description at step 8, and the commit adds only the merge's parents. A conflict
    is found by a check, not by eye.
  - The landed tree differs from the reviewed one only when the trunk moved during the cycle, the
    merge then bringing in commits no validation saw. Land's sync rule already stops that, and
    `--land` enforces it before anything moves: no conflict, `REV` local equal to its remote and
    the ladder forked from it, and `REV` a bookmark, since `--land` moves it.
  - Then the closing, the fast-forward of `REV`, the push of the trunk with the agent journal as
    its partner, and the topic bookmark's deletion, `--skip local|remote|both` keeping what it
    names. Whether the install joins it is settled at the rung, the install not being a `jj` step.
  - Set aside: a separate `land` command, and `push --land`, the agent's proposal, both of which
    kept a review between the closing and its Land that adds nothing.
- `commit` pushes what it commits, wink's model at the closing rung (2026-10-23): closing a cycle
  means its local and remote topic bookmarks both end on the closing, and every commit pushed at
  once is durable and is what the cycles have done all along, so pushing is the default, one rule.
  - The push is today's `push -s b` run after the commit in the same invocation: the agent half
    committed or folded as the partner, an empty one included, and the topic bookmark set and
    pushed. With `--land` the topic push is skipped, `main` moving instead.
  - `--no-push` keeps one commit local and `--push` forces the push, over `[commit] push`, `true`
    or `false`, `true` when absent, so a project or a person choosing the local pause sets it
    once. The flag, then the key, then `true`, printed as every default is.
  - The pause v0.3.1 put between the commit and its push, a look at the commit itself, goes by
    default, the argument `--land` accepted: the diff is reviewed at step 6 and the description at
    step 8, and the commit adds only the trailer and a closing's parents. The per-push approval
    moves onto the commit, the go at step 8 covering the commit and its push, steps 8 and 9 one.
    A `--no-push` commit keeps the pause, so the rules name both, proposal material for v0.3.1's
    per-rung flow.
- `push <bookmark>` publishes a bookmark whose commit is committed, the working copy being the one
  node it refuses, pointing at `commit`, wink's call (2026-10-23).
  - A committed node is pushable whether or not jj calls it immutable, so a `--no-push` commit is
    published later by `push`, and a pair's work half still has its agent partner completed as
    today. The docs and errors say "committed", since jj's "immutable", a commit it refuses to
    rewrite, is narrower.
- `vc-x1 reparent`, wink's call at the closing rung's review (2026-10-23): parent fix-ups get their
  own command, since `merge` is the wrong verb for removing one.
  - `--target <REV>`, any committed node, with `--add`, `--remove`, or `--set`, one jj-lib rebase
    of it onto its new parent list, its descendants rebased, the list printed before and after,
    and a failure restored from a snapshot. `merge`'s guards carry over: no cycle, no parent at or
    below the target, `--ignore-immutable` for a jj-immutable one.
  - `--remove` changes the tree: the target keeps its own diff, and what the removed parent brought
    is gone from it, so it prints what was dropped. The last parent is never removed, `--set`
    being the way to replace it, and a conflicted result is reported and left.
  - `merge` stays as the short form of `--add`, its tests and `commit --closing`'s use of its
    primitive unchanged, and may retire into `reparent` later.
- `commit -s a`, wink's call (2026-10-23): the agent repo is committed alone when asked, an
  unpaired commit with the given title and body and no trailer, `--push` publishing its `main`.
  - The refusal it replaces guarded a paired agent commit made before its work half. An unpaired
    one names no partner, so nothing mismatches. An agent `@` that is a pending partner keeps its
    change id when committed, so the work commit's trailer still resolves, and a warning says the
    back-trailer is missing.
  - The principle, wink's (2026-10-23): do what the user asks unless it is dangerous, and warn
    rather than refuse, so a fix-up such as a repaired change id stays inside `vc-x1`.
- The closing's undo is in this cycle, the Todo's lean, for a closing made without `--land`, a flag
  or a sibling command settled at its rung. A Land's undo, after its push, waits for a real mistake.
- Bookmark deletion is a rung of this cycle, not its own cycle, since `--land` and `--skip` use it.
- Multi-step, fourteen work rungs between the bookends, the closing and landing path first, since each
  of its rungs is used by the next, then the four steps the widening added.

#### Problem

A cycle's multi-step operations are typed as raw `jj` commands in order, and each is a place to
make a mistake: the opening's `jj git push --named` creating and publishing the bookmark, the
closing, Land's sync, fast-forward, push, and two `jj` lines deleting the bookmark, the reshape of
a draft bookmark, the coordinated re-describe, local ladders, and setting a rung's edits aside, any
of them able to skip the sync, move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. The goal, wink's
(2026-10-23), is that no cycle step needs `jj` typed by hand for these operations. `commit
--closing` assumed `main`, was tested on a ladder of two rungs only, and refused a single-step
cycle, and a closing made by mistake is undone by hand in two repos.

#### Solution

Provisional. Each multi-step operation of a cycle becomes one `vc-x1` invocation that checks before
it acts and prints what it resolved:

- `commit --opening <BOOKMARK>` creates and pushes the bookmark at `@-` and makes the opening,
  appending " opening" to the bare title, and every commit advances the line's bookmark locally.
- `commit` pushes what it commits by default, `--no-push` or `[commit] push = false` keeping it
  local, and `push <bookmark>` publishes a bookmark on a committed node.
- `commit --closing <REV>` closes every cycle shape onto the named revision, its title and body
  derived from the opening and the config. A branch of one node is finalized in place, the bare
  title replacing the opening's. A longer one gets a closing commit, titled " closing", or
  " dead-end closing" with `--dead-end`, a trapezoid or linear, from `--shape`, else `[cycle]
  closing-shape`, else trapezoid, converting between them while it is a draft. With `[record]`
  set, the record moves from the doing file to the closed file. A closing can be taken back in
  both repos at once.
- `commit --closing <REV> --land` also lands it: the fast-forward of `REV`, the push, and the
  bookmark's deletion, refused when the trunk moved or the merge conflicts.
- `vc-x1` deletes a bookmark locally and remotely, `--skip` keeping either side.
- `vc-x1` reshapes a draft bookmark, edits a commit's parents with `reparent`, re-describes a pair
  keeping its trailers, runs a local ladder,
  and sets a rung's edits aside and back.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with tests for:

- `commit --closing` finalizing a one-node branch in place, and closing ladders of two and three
  nodes, each shape from the flag, from the key, and by default, the title and body derived, the
  record moved with `[record]` set and left without, the conversion each way, the closing's undo
  restoring both repos, and `--land` landing a single-step cycle, a trapezoid, and a linear ladder
  on fixtures and refusing a moved trunk, a conflict, a revision that is not a bookmark, and a
  commit of none of those shapes.
- `commit --opening` creating and pushing the bookmark, each `--skip`, the title suffix, and the
  line's bookmark advancing.
- `commit` pushing by default, `--no-push` and `[commit] push` keeping it local, `-s a` committing
  the agent repo alone, and `push <bookmark>` publishing a committed node and refusing the working
  copy.
- Bookmark deletion, the reshape, `reparent` adding, removing, and setting parents, the
  re-describe, the local ladder, and the set-aside.

This cycle's own Land is run by the dev build's `commit --closing main --land`, its report showing
`main` and `main@origin` at the closing and the bookmark gone locally and remotely, and the
installed `vc-x1 -V` a bare 0.85.8.

#### Ladder

  straight history, a linear closing is a plain commit on the ladder, and `--land` fast-forwards
  `REV` to it, the agent-files' keep separate under a clearer name.
  - `--shape <trapezoid|linear>` chooses it, one valued flag rather than `--linear` and
    `--trapezoid`, which could both be given, or abbreviations such as `--clse-lin`, which read as

  - `[cycle] closing-shape`, `"trapezoid"` or `"linear"`, is the project's default, a preference
    that belongs in the committed `.vc-config.md` with `[validate]` and `[build]`, since adopters

    refused.

    published commits into a tree no validation saw. `--land` already refuses a moved trunk, so
    the refusal is the whole answer, and the way out is the reshape rung's command, then a
    validation, then the closing. A rebase inside a linear closing would be the hidden multi-step
    operation this cycle removes.

    linear, and converts** now keeps it as the linear shape and names the flag and the key, edited

    rung.

    step 6 and its description at step 8, and the commit adds only the merge's parents. A conflict
    is found by a check, not by eye.

    merge then bringing in commits no validation saw. Land's sync rule already stops that, and
    `--land` enforces it before anything moves: no conflict, `REV` local equal to its remote and
    the ladder forked from it, and `REV` a bookmark, since `--land` moves it.
  - Then the closing, the fast-forward of `REV`, the push of the trunk with the agent journal as
    its partner, and the topic bookmark's deletion, `--skip local|remote|both` keeping what it
    names. Whether the install joins it is settled at the rung, the install not being a `jj` step.
  - Set aside: a separate `land` command, and `push --land`, the agent's proposal, both of which
    kept a review between the closing and its Land that adds nothing.
- `commit` pushes what it commits, wink's model at the closing rung (2026-10-23): closing a cycle
  means its local and remote topic bookmarks both end on the closing, and every commit pushed at
  once is durable and is what the cycles have done all along, so pushing is the default, one rule.

    committed or folded as the partner, an empty one included, and the topic bookmark set and
    pushed. With `--land` the topic push is skipped, `main` moving instead.
  - `--no-push` keeps one commit local and `--push` forces the push, over `[commit] push`, `true`
    or `false`, `true` when absent, so a project or a person choosing the local pause sets it
    once. The flag, then the key, then `true`, printed as every default is.
  - The pause v0.3.1 put between the commit and its push, a look at the commit itself, goes by
    default, the argument `--land` accepted: the diff is reviewed at step 6 and the description at
    step 8, and the commit adds only the trailer and a closing's parents. The per-push approval
    moves onto the commit, the go at step 8 covering the commit and its push, steps 8 and 9 one.

    per-rung flow.

  node it refuses, pointing at `commit`, wink's call (2026-10-23).

    published later by `push`, and a pair's work half still has its agent partner completed as
    today. The docs and errors say "committed", since jj's "immutable", a commit it refuses to
    rewrite, is narrower.

    and a failure restored from a snapshot. `merge`'s guards carry over: no cycle, no parent at or
    below the target, `--ignore-immutable` for a jj-immutable one.

    is gone from it, so it prints what was dropped. The last parent is never removed, `--set`
    being the way to replace it, and a conflicted result is reported and left.

  unpaired commit with the given title and body and no trailer, `--push` publishing its `main`.

    back-trailer is missing.

  or a sibling command settled at its rung. A Land's undo, after its push, waits for a real mistake.

- Multi-step, fourteen work rungs between the bookends, the closing and landing path first, since each
  of its rungs is used by the next, then the four steps the widening added.

#### Problem

A cycle's multi-step operations are typed as raw `jj` commands in order, and each is a place to
make a mistake: the opening's `jj git push --named` creating and publishing the bookmark, the
closing, Land's sync, fast-forward, push, and two `jj` lines deleting the bookmark, the reshape of
a draft bookmark, the coordinated re-describe, local ladders, and setting a rung's edits aside, any
of them able to skip the sync, move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. The goal, wink's
(2026-10-23), is that no cycle step needs `jj` typed by hand for these operations. `commit
--closing` assumed `main`, was tested on a ladder of two rungs only, and refused a single-step
cycle, and a closing made by mistake is undone by hand in two repos.

Provisional. Each multi-step operation of a cycle becomes one `vc-x1` invocation that checks before
it acts and prints what it resolved:

  appending " opening" to the bare title, and every commit advances the line's bookmark locally.
- `commit` pushes what it commits by default, `--no-push` or `[commit] push = false` keeping it
  local, and `push <bookmark>` publishes a bookmark on a committed node.
- `commit --closing <REV>` closes every cycle shape onto the named revision, its title and body
  derived from the opening and the config. A branch of one node is finalized in place, the bare
  title replacing the opening's. A longer one gets a closing commit, titled " closing", or
  " dead-end closing" with `--dead-end`, a trapezoid or linear, from `--shape`, else `[cycle]
  closing-shape`, else trapezoid, converting between them while it is a draft. With `[record]`
  set, the record moves from the doing file to the closed file. A closing can be taken back in
  both repos at once.
- `commit --closing <REV> --land` also lands it: the fast-forward of `REV`, the push, and the
  bookmark's deletion, refused when the trunk moved or the merge conflicts.
- `vc-x1` deletes a bookmark locally and remotely, `--skip` keeping either side.
- `vc-x1` reshapes a draft bookmark, edits a commit's parents with `reparent`, re-describes a pair
  keeping its trailers, runs a local ladder,
  and sets a rung's edits aside and back.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with tests for:

- `commit --closing` finalizing a one-node branch in place, and closing ladders of two and three
  nodes, each shape from the flag, from the key, and by default, the title and body derived, the
  record moved with `[record]` set and left without, the conversion each way, the closing's undo
  restoring both repos, and `--land` landing a single-step cycle, a trapezoid, and a linear ladder
  on fixtures and refusing a moved trunk, a conflict, a revision that is not a bookmark, and a
  commit of none of those shapes.
- `commit --opening` creating and pushing the bookmark, each `--skip`, the title suffix, and the
  line's bookmark advancing.
- `commit` pushing by default, `--no-push` and `[commit] push` keeping it local, `-s a` committing
  the agent repo alone, and `push <bookmark>` publishing a committed node and refusing the working
  copy.
- Bookmark deletion, the reshape, `reparent` adding, removing, and setting parents, the
  re-describe, the local ladder, and the set-aside.

`main` and `main@origin` at the closing and the bookmark gone locally and remotely, and the
installed `vc-x1 -V` a bare 0.85.8.

  own command, since `merge` is the wrong verb for removing one.

    of it onto its new parent list, its descendants rebased, the list printed before and after,
    and a failure restored from a snapshot. `merge`'s guards carry over: no cycle, no parent at or
    below the target, `--ignore-immutable` for a jj-immutable one.
  - `--remove` changes the tree: the target keeps its own diff, and what the removed parent brought
    is gone from it, so it prints what was dropped. The last parent is never removed, `--set`
    being the way to replace it, and a conflicted result is reported and left.
  - `merge` stays as the short form of `--add`, its tests and `commit --closing`'s use of its
    primitive unchanged, and may retire into `reparent` later.

## commit.push

Whether `vc-x1 commit` pushes what it commits in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push` would after
it. True is the default, every commit published as soon as it is made: `--no-push` keeps one commit
local and `--push` pushes one when the key is false. A commit with `--no-advance` pushes only with
`--push`, since its bookmark was left where it was. Owned by the work side because the commits are
the work repo's.

```toml
[commit.push]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "bool"
doc = "Default for commit: push what it commits, `--no-push` / `--push` override"
used-by = "vc-x1 commit --push / --no-push"
default = true
```

A model config file: every table and key a workspace config may carry, each with its default or a
typical value. Generated from the schema, so it cannot fall behind the keys the binary knows. Copy
the tables you need into your own `.vc-config.md` and drop the rest.

The values inside a `toml` fence are the workspace's own, and the prose around them is
documentation. Only a fence tagged exactly `toml` is read, so any other fence is prose like the
text beside it. Each bullet links to its key's entry in the schema documentation.

The `[agent-session]` table
- items: Default agent-session item set (comma-separated) [[1]]
- result-lines: Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 = unlimited) [[2]]
- col-width: Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown / --per-line views
  [[3]]
```toml
[agent-session]
items = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
result-lines = 10
col-width = 68
```

The `[repos]` table
- work: The work repo's path, relative to this config file's directory ("." in the work repo, ".."
  in the agent repo). The entry resolving to the config's own directory names the side [[4]]
- agent: The agent repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (e.g. ".agent-session" in
  the work repo, "." in the agent repo). Presence signals dual-repo mode [[5]]
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".agent-session"
```

The `[remote]` table
- agent-repo: The agent-repo's name on its remote, the last URL segment only, since the owner and
  host come from the work-repo's remote. Absent means a name derived from repos.agent: a dot-led
  last component appended to the work repo's name, any other used whole [[6]]
```toml
[remote]
agent-repo = "myproject.agent-session"
```

The `[family]` table
- member: This repo's member name in its agent-file family (also its record file in the messages
  repo) [[7]]
- template: Path to the family's template payload, the directory holding the pinned agent-files
  [[8]]
- messages: Path to the family's messages repo, relative to this config file's directory [[9]]
```toml
[family]
member = "vc-x1"
template = "../vc-x1-template/work"
messages = "../vc-x1-messages"
```

The `[agent-files.diff]` table
- dir: Default DIR for agent-files diff: a directory holding a copy of the set [[10]]
- custom: Default for agent-files diff --custom: compare custom.md like the rest of the set [[11]]
```toml
[agent-files.diff]
dir = "../iiac-perf"
custom = false
```

The `[agent-files.copy]` table
- dir: Default DIR for agent-files copy: a directory holding a copy of the set [[12]]
- custom: Default for agent-files copy --custom: copy custom.md with the rest of the set [[13]]
```toml
[agent-files.copy]
dir = "../vc-x1-template/work"
custom = false
```

The `[squash-push]` table
- yes: Default for squash-push: act without asking once the precheck found work [[14]]
```toml
[squash-push]
yes = true
```

The `[validate]` table
- full: Full validation, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 validate` [[15]]
- fast: Fast validation, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 validate --fast` [[16]]
```toml
[validate]
full = [
  "cargo fmt",
  "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings",
  "cargo test -- --include-ignored",
]
fast = ["cargo test --bins"]
```

The `[build]` table
- release: The release build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build` [[17]]
- release-bin: The release build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run` and copied by `vc-x1 install` [[18]]
- dev: The dev build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build-dev` [[19]]
- dev-bin: The dev build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run-dev` and copied by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[20]]
```toml

```

- release-dir: Where `vc-x1 install` copies the release build, `~` expanded [[22]]
- dev: Optional, the dev install run by `vc-x1 install-dev` in place of its own copy [[23]]
- dev-dir: Where `vc-x1 install-dev` copies the dev build, `~` expanded [[24]]
- dev-suffix: Appended to the dev build's file name by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[25]]

 right: "# vc-x1 config file

A model config file: every table and key a workspace config may carry, each with its default or a
typical value. Generated from the schema, so it cannot fall behind the keys the binary knows. Copy
the tables you need into your own `.vc-config.md` and drop the rest.

The values inside a `toml` fence are the workspace's own, and the prose around them is
documentation. Only a fence tagged exactly `toml` is read, so any other fence is prose like the
text beside it. Each bullet links to its key's entry in the schema documentation.

The `[agent-session]` table
- items: Default agent-session item set (comma-separated) [[1]]
- result-lines: Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 = unlimited) [[2]]
- col-width: Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown / --per-line views
  [[3]]
```toml
[agent-session]
items = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
result-lines = 10
col-width = 68
```

The `[repos]` table
- work: The work repo's path, relative to this config file's directory ("." in the work repo, ".."
  in the agent repo). The entry resolving to the config's own directory names the side [[4]]
- agent: The agent repo's path, relative to this config file's directory (e.g. ".agent-session" in
  the work repo, "." in the agent repo). Presence signals dual-repo mode [[5]]
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".agent-session"
```

The `[remote]` table
- agent-repo: The agent-repo's name on its remote, the last URL segment only, since the owner and
  host come from the work-repo's remote. Absent means a name derived from repos.agent: a dot-led
  last component appended to the work repo's name, any other used whole [[6]]
```toml
[remote]
agent-repo = "myproject.agent-session"
```

The `[family]` table
- member: This repo's member name in its agent-file family (also its record file in the messages
  repo) [[7]]
- template: Path to the family's template payload, the directory holding the pinned agent-files
  [[8]]
- messages: Path to the family's messages repo, relative to this config file's directory [[9]]
```toml
[family]
member = "vc-x1"
template = "../vc-x1-template/work"
messages = "../vc-x1-messages"
```

The `[agent-files.diff]` table
- dir: Default DIR for agent-files diff: a directory holding a copy of the set [[10]]
- custom: Default for agent-files diff --custom: compare custom.md like the rest of the set [[11]]
```toml
[agent-files.diff]
dir = "../iiac-perf"
custom = false
```

The `[agent-files.copy]` table
- dir: Default DIR for agent-files copy: a directory holding a copy of the set [[12]]
- custom: Default for agent-files copy --custom: copy custom.md with the rest of the set [[13]]
```toml
[agent-files.copy]
dir = "../vc-x1-template/work"
custom = false
```

The `[squash-push]` table
- yes: Default for squash-push: act without asking once the precheck found work [[14]]
```toml
[squash-push]
yes = true
```

The `[validate]` table
- full: Full validation, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 validate` [[15]]
- fast: Fast validation, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 validate --fast` [[16]]
```toml
[validate]
full = [
  "cargo fmt",
  "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings",
  "cargo test -- --include-ignored",
]
fast = ["cargo test --bins"]
```

The `[build]` table
- release: The release build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build` [[17]]
- release-bin: The release build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run` and copied by `vc-x1 install` [[18]]
- dev: The dev build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build-dev` [[19]]
- dev-bin: The dev build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run-dev` and copied by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[20]]
```toml
[build]
release = ["cargo build --release --locked"]
release-bin = "target/release/vc-x1"
dev = ["cargo build --locked"]
dev-bin = "target/debug/vc-x1"
```

The `[install]` table
- release: Optional, the release install run by `vc-x1 install` in place of its own copy [[21]]
- release-dir: Where `vc-x1 install` copies the release build, `~` expanded [[22]]
- dev: Optional, the dev install run by `vc-x1 install-dev` in place of its own copy [[23]]
- dev-dir: Where `vc-x1 install-dev` copies the dev build, `~` expanded [[24]]
- dev-suffix: Appended to the dev build's file name by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[25]]
```toml
[install]
release = [
  "cp {build.release-bin} {install.release-dir}/vc-x1.new",
  "mv {install.release-dir}/vc-x1.new {install.release-dir}/vc-x1",
]
release-dir = "~/.cargo/bin"
dev = [
  "cp {build.dev-bin} {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}.new",
  "mv {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}.new {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}",
]
dev-dir = "~/.cargo/bin"
dev-suffix = "-dev"
```

The `[commit]` table
- push: Default for commit: push what it commits, `--no-push` / `--push` override [[26]]
```toml
[commit]
push = true
```

The `[closing]` table
- body: The closing commit's default body, `{title}` the cycle title [[27]]
```toml
[closing]
body = "Closes the cycle {title}. See details in zCLOSED.md."
```

The `[test]` table
- fixtures: Directory of the acceptance-test fixtures, one dual workspace per name, read by `cargo
  test` [[28]]
```toml
[test]
fixtures = ".fixtures"
```

- release-bin: The release build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run` and copied by `vc-x1 install` [[18]]
- dev: The dev build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build-dev` [[19]]
- dev-bin: The dev build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run-dev` and copied by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[20]]
```toml
[build]
release = ["cargo build --release --locked"]
release-bin = "target/release/vc-x1"
dev = ["cargo build --locked"]
dev-bin = "target/debug/vc-x1"
```

The `[install]` table
- release: Optional, the release install run by `vc-x1 install` in place of its own copy [[21]]
- release-dir: Where `vc-x1 install` copies the release build, `~` expanded [[22]]
- dev: Optional, the dev install run by `vc-x1 install-dev` in place of its own copy [[23]]
- dev-dir: Where `vc-x1 install-dev` copies the dev build, `~` expanded [[24]]
- dev-suffix: Appended to the dev build's file name by `vc-x1 install-dev` [[25]]
```toml
[install]
release = [
  "cp {build.release-bin} {install.release-dir}/vc-x1.new",
  "mv {install.release-dir}/vc-x1.new {install.release-dir}/vc-x1",
]
release-dir = "~/.cargo/bin"
dev = [
  "cp {build.dev-bin} {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}.new",
  "mv {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}.new {install.dev-dir}/vc-x1{install.dev-suffix}",
]
dev-dir = "~/.cargo/bin"
dev-suffix = "-dev"
```

The `[commit]` table
- push: Default for commit: push what it commits, `--no-push` / `--push` override [[26]]
```toml
[commit]
push = true
```

The `[closing]` table
- body: The closing commit's default body, `{title}` the cycle title [[27]]
```toml
[closing]
body = "Closes the cycle {title}. See details in zCLOSED.md."
```

The `[test]` table
- fixtures: Directory of the acceptance-test fixtures, one dual workspace per name, read by `cargo
  test` [[28]]
```toml
[test]
fixtures = ".fixtures"
```

content.content:
### commit

Commit the working copies as a rung's pair: one commit per repo of a dual workspace, each stamped
with the other's change id, before anything is pushed. The pair is what the per-rung flow reviews,
description and diff together, by `vc-x1 show -s both @-`, so a fix after the review folds into
the pair and never rewrites a remote, and `push` publishes what was reviewed. Both change ids are
known before either commit is made, since a jj commit keeps the working copy's change id, so each
trailer is written once.

### push

Publish a rung's pair. Push carries no description and writes none, so what was reviewed is what
goes out: `commit` makes the pair, the work commit and the agent commit each naming the other, or
the work half alone with its trailer naming the agent `@`, and push completes and publishes it.

```bash
vc-x1 push -s b                  # the pair, on the bookmark the work @- sits on
vc-x1 push -s b feature          # the same, the bookmark named as a check
vc-x1 push -s w                  # the work half only
vc-x1 push -s a                  # the agent half only, the remainder of a run that stopped
vc-x1 push -s p -R ../other      # a plain repo's @- on its bookmark, no trailer asked for
vc-x1 push -s b --dry-run        # plan and print, move nothing
```

What push refuses, with both repos as they were:

- a work `@` that is not empty: unsquashed work is a fix to fold or the next rung, the user's call
- a work `@-` with no `ochid:` trailer: not a pair's commit, so `commit` makes one first
- a named bookmark that is not on the line `@-` is on, or two bookmarks on the line and none named

The two halves are independent, since each trailer is fixed before push runs, so `push -s b` is
